claim_boundary: This artifact proves that every collision forces a continued-fraction convergent and a fixed-power next partial quotient. It proves no averaged jump theorem, collision or simple-root closure, complete moment, density, or intervals.

continued_fraction_jump_theorem.averaged_target: for every dyadic M, it suffices to show that at most O((Q/M)X^epsilon) modes a have a convergent q<<Q/M whose next partial quotient is >>KM^2/Q
continued_fraction_jump_theorem.boundary: no averaged large-partial-quotient theorem, collision or simple-root closure, complete moment, density, or prime intervals is proved
continued_fraction_jump_theorem.collision_input: for alpha=g^a, a reduced collision label p/q satisfies |alpha-p/q|<<1/(KQ) and q<<Q/M
continued_fraction_jump_theorem.legendre: 2q^2|alpha-p/q|<<Q/(KM^2)=X^(-(xi+2mu-1/3)); the minimum margin is 23/75, so Legendre's criterion makes p/q a continued-fraction convergent uniformly
continued_fraction_jump_theorem.next_denominator: q_next>1/(q|alpha-p/q|)-q>>KM; the subtraction is absorbed by the same positive Legendre margin
continued_fraction_jump_theorem.partial_quotient: q_next=A_next q+q_previous forces A_next>>KM^2/Q, with X-exponent xi+2mu-1/3>=23/75

remaining_target.statement: bound the number of exponential modes with a convergent followed by a partial quotient >>KM^2/Q, or classify their common structure
